title: China production-input prices mostly declined in early August
summary: China's monitored production-input basket moved broadly lower in the period, with 31 of 50 products declining and 12 increasing. The distribution provides a useful watchpoint for industrial input costs.
what_happened: 31 of 50 monitored products decreased in price.
interpretation: The monitored basket shows broad downward price movement rather than a uniform shift. These are market prices for important means of production and do not by themselves establish producer prices, export prices or Canadian landed costs.

title: China retail sales grew 0.6% in July
summary: China's retail economy expanded only modestly in July, although growth excluding automobiles was stronger. The divergence suggests consumer demand is uneven rather than uniformly weak.
what_happened: Total retail sales of consumer goods 0.6% YoY (July).
Of which: Retail sales of consumer goods excluding automobiles 2.5% YoY (July).
Total retail sales of consumer goods 1.2% YoY (January - July).
Of which: Retail sales of consumer goods excluding automobiles 2.7% YoY (January - July).
Of which: Retail sales of enterprises (units) above the designated size -3.4% YoY (July).
interpretation: Retail growth remained weak overall, but performance varied materially across categories. Stronger growth outside automobiles indicates that the softness in headline retail activity is not uniform across consumer demand.
canadian_relevance: Canadian businesses exposed to Chinese consumer demand should watch which categories are expanding and which remain weak, particularly where China is an important market or competitor.

title: China industrial output grew 4.5% in July
summary: China's industrial sector continued to expand in July, with manufacturing growth remaining solid and high-tech manufacturing significantly outperforming the broader sector. For businesses exposed to Chinese industrial supply or demand, the divergence across sectors matters more than the headline rate alone.
what_happened: Value Added of Industrial Enterprises Above the Designated Size 4.5% YoY (July).
Value Added of Industrial Enterprises Above the Designated Size 5.3% YoY (January-July).
interpretation: Industrial output continued to grow, but the sector mix was uneven. High-tech manufacturing materially outpaced the broader industrial sector while mining contracted in July, indicating that industrial momentum is concentrated in particular parts of the economy.

canadian_relevance: Canadian exporters, suppliers and competitors should watch where Chinese industrial growth is accelerating, particularly in high-tech manufacturing, because stronger domestic production can affect input demand, competitive pricing and supply-chain opportunities.

Industrial Production Operation in July 2026 2026-08-18 15:00 Print | Large | Medium | Small In July, the total value added of industrial enterprises above the designated size increased by 4.5% year on year in real terms (the growth rates of value added are the real growth rates after deducting price factors).

In July, the product sales ratio of industrial enterprises above the designated size was 96.9%, a year-on-year decrease of 0.6 percentage points; and the export delivery value realized by industrial enterprises above the designated size was 1,413.3 billion yuan, a nominal increase of 10.4% year on year.
Product sales ratio: refers to the ratio of sales value to total industrial output value, which reflects the coordination between production and sales of industrial products.

In terms of three sectors, in July, the value added of the mining industry decreased by 4.2% year on year, that of the manufacturing industry increased by 5.5%, and that of the production and supply of electricity, heat power, gas and water increased by 5.0%.
In terms of products, in July, the output of 279 out of 626 products produced by industrial enterprises above the designated size increased year on year.

Notes on Indicators Growth rate of total value added of industrial enterprises: also known as industrial growth rate, is used to reflect the degree of increase or decrease in industrial output over a given period.
Survey Method Statistics on industrial production of enterprises above the designated size are collected through a comprehensive monthly survey (with reporting exempted for January).
